parole.significato: The end of a sari that hangs loose over the shoulder.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi आँचल (ā̃cal), from Sanskrit अञ्चल (añcala).

parole.significato: A particular Hindu prayer ritual, involving candles made from clarified butter.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi आरती (ārtī), from Sanskrit आरात्रिक (ārātrika).

parole.significato: agarwood
parole.testo: Possibly from Hindi अगर (agar), from Sanskrit अगरु (agaru).

parole.significato: A period of concealment or exile of the Pandavas.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi अज्ञातवास (ajñātvās), from Sanskrit अज्ञातवास (ajñātavāsa), from अज्ञात (ajñāta, “unknown”) and वास (vāsa, “staying”).

parole.significato: A member of a clan or community, mostly in northern India, whose traditional occupations are cattle-herding and agricul…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi अहीर (ahīr), from Sanskrit आभीर (ābhīra).

parole.significato: A plant related to ajwain, Trachyspermum roxburghianum, used as a spice and in Ayurvedic medicine.
parole.testo: Probably from Hindi अजमोद (ajmod) from Sanskrit अजमोद (ajamoda)

parole.significato: One of the four margas (traditional techniques for playing percussive intruments), which combines strokes of the vamaka…
parole.testo: Possibly from Hindi or Sanskrit.

parole.significato: The hooked goad that is used in India to control elephants.
parole.testo: From Hindi अंकुस (aṅkus)/अंकुश (aṅkuś), from Sanskrit अङ्कुश (aṅkuśa).

parole.significato: A former Indian coin, being a 16th of a rupee.
parole.testo: From Hindi अन्न (ann, “food, grain”), आना (ānā), from Sanskrit अन्न (anna).

parole.significato: a class of female celestial beings, originally associated with waters and clouds and later especially with celestial da…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi अप्सरा (apsarā), descended from Sanskrit अप्सरस् (apsaras).

parole.significato: A tropical fruit tree from India, Aegle marmelos.
parole.testo: From Hindi बेल (bel), from Sanskrit बिल्व (bilva), विल्व (vilva), or बैल्व (bailva).

parole.significato: A large kerchief, usually colourful and used either as headgear or as a handkerchief, neckerchief, bikini, or sweatband.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi बंधन (bandhan, “the act of binding, a bond”), from Sanskrit बध्नाति (badhnāti, “he binds”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰendʰ- (“to bind, bond”). Related to Hindi बाँधना (bāndhnā, “to tie”). Doublet of bind.

parole.significato: A general strike, shutdown, or other form of protest used in South Asia in which a substantial portion of the populatio…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi बंध (bandh, “closure”), from Sanskrit बन्ध (bandha). Doublet of bund (“a type of enclosure”).

parole.significato: A warehouse.
parole.testo: From Hindi भंडसाल (bhaṇḍsāl), from Sanskrit भाण्डशाला (bhāṇḍaśālā): भाण्ड (bhāṇḍa, “goods”) + शाला (śālā, “house, building”). Altered by folk etymology in English after bank, hall.

parole.significato: Synonym of okra: the plant or its edible capsules.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi भिंडी (bhiṇḍī, “okra”), a feminine form of Sanskrit भिण्डा (bhiṇḍā).

parole.significato: A supernatural creature, usually the ghost of a deceased person.
parole.testo: From Hindi भूत (bhūt), from Sanskrit भूत (bhūta).

parole.significato: Synonym of false daisy.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi भृङ्गराज (bhŕṅgarāj), from Sanskrit भृङ्गराज (bhṛṅgarāja).

parole.significato: A poison extracted from Aconitum ferox or related species of.
parole.testo: From Hindi बिख (bikh, “poison”), from Sanskrit विष (viṣa, “poison”).

parole.significato: A merchant or trader.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi बनिया (baniyā), ultimately from Sanskrit वणिज् (vaṇij). Doublet of banyan.

parole.significato: A small two-wheeled vehicle drawn by two oxen.
parole.testo: From Hindi बहली (bahlī), from Sanskrit वह् (vah, “to carry”).

parole.significato: A flat, unleavened bread from northern India and Pakistan.
parole.testo: From Hindi चपाती (capātī), from Sanskrit चर्पटी (carpaṭī). From a derivative of Sanskrit *चर्प (carpa, “flat”).

parole.significato: Synonym of umbrella or parasol, particularly an Indian parasol.
parole.testo: From Hindi छाता (chātā), from Sanskrit छत्त्र (chattra, “umbrella, parasol, chatra”). Doublet of chador and chatra.

parole.significato: A distinctive member (Acinonyx jubatus) of the cat family, slightly smaller than the leopard, but with proportionately…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi चीता (cītā, “leopard, panther”), ultimately from Sanskrit चित्र (citra, “multicolored, speckled”) (akin to Old High German haitar (“bright”) > German heiter; Old Norse heiðr (“bright”)) + Sanskrit काय (kāya, “body”), thus “having a spotted body”.

parole.significato: A kind of felwort, Swertia chirata (syn. Agathotes chirayta), found in northern India, esteemed as a tonic and febrifug…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi चिरैता (ciraitā), from Sanskrit किराततिक्त (kirātatikta).

parole.significato: a large spotted deer, of genus Axis, native to India and Sri Lanka
parole.testo: From Hindi चीतल (cītal), from Sanskrit चित्रल (citrala, “variegated, spotted”) from Sanskrit चित्र (citra, “spotted, bright; spot, mark”).

parole.significato: An intersection or roundabout, where tracks or roads cross (often used in place names).
parole.testo: From Hindi चौक (cauk, “plaza, square, courtyard”), from Sanskrit चतुष्क (catuṣka, “quadrangular courtyard, crossway”).

parole.significato: A flyflap or whisk originally made from the bushy tail of a yak.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi चौंरी (ca͠urī), from Sanskrit चमर (camara, “yak”).

parole.significato: A bird of species of partridge native to central Asia (Alectoris chukar).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi चकोर (cakor), from Sanskrit चकोर (cakora).

parole.significato: Any of the six playing periods, each 7½ minutes long, of a game of polo.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi चक्कर (cakkar), from Sanskrit चक्र (cakra). Doublet of chakra, chakram, charkha, cycle, cyclus, kike, and wheel.

parole.significato: A wet nurse; a midwife.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi दाई (dāī), from Sanskrit.

parole.significato: A Hindu temple or mandir.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi देवल (deval), in turn from Sanskrit देवकुल (devakula).

parole.significato: A charitable or religious house, especially a resthouse for travellers.
parole.testo: From Hindi धर्मशाला (dharmaśālā), from Sanskrit.

parole.significato: A type of drum from India.
parole.testo: From Hindi ढोल (ḍhol), from Sanskrit ढोल (ḍhola).

parole.significato: A form of extruded Indian incense, lacking a core bamboo stick.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi धूप (dhūp), from Sanskrit धूप (dhūpa), from धूप् (dhūp, “to fumigate, perfume”, root) + Proto-Indo-European *-os.

parole.significato: A caste (or member of this caste) in Indian society, originally comprising drummers or travelling musicians and now gen…
parole.testo: From Hindi [Term?], from Sanskrit डोम (ḍoma). Doublet of Rom.

parole.significato: Synonym of Bermuda grass.
parole.testo: From Hindi दूब (dūb), from Sanskrit दूर्वा (dūrvā). The first element is a doublet of durva.

parole.significato: A basic Indian litter or sedan chair made of poles, ropes, and a seat or cloth.
parole.testo: From Hindi डोली (ḍolī), from डोला (ḍolā, “litter”) + -ई (-ī, “forming diminutives”), from Sanskrit दोल (dōlā, “dangling cradle; litter”), from दुल् (dul, “to swing”). Compare andor from Sanskrit हिन्दोल (hindola) via Portuguese.

parole.significato: Marijuana, the inflorescence of the Cannabis sativa plant, smoked or ingested for euphoric effect.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi गांजा (gāñjā), ultimately from Sanskrit गञ्जा (gañjā, “hemp”). First use appears c. 1800.

parole.significato: An Asian species of wild bovine (Bos gaurus), of large size and an untamable disposition.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi गौर (gaur), from Sanskrit गौर (gaura). Attested in English since the early 19th century. Doublet of gayal.

parole.significato: A long ornamented skirt or petticoat, tightened with a drawstring and often hung with bells, worn in Rajasthan and othe…
parole.testo: From Hindi घाघरा (ghāghrā), from Sanskrit [Term?].

parole.significato: An animal shelter for stray cows, which are sacred in Hinduism.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi गोशाला (gośālā), from Sanskrit गोशाला (gośālā).

parole.significato: An annual legume (Cyamopsis tetragonoloba), used as a food for cattle and humans.
parole.testo: From Hindi ग्वार (gvār), from Sanskrit गोपाली (gopālī, “kind of cucumber”), shortened from गोपालकर्कटी (gopālakarkaṭī, “cowherder's cucumber”), from गोपाल (gopāla, “cowherd”) + कर्कटी (karkaṭī, “cucumber”) (see Latin cucumis and cucurbita).

parole.significato: Commiphora wightii, a flowering plant most common in northern India, with thin papery bark and thorny branches.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi गूगल (gūgal), from Sanskrit गुल्गु॒लु॒ (gúlgulu).

parole.significato: A member of a nomadic and agricultural community of India, Pakistan and Afghanistan.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi गूजर (gūjar), from Sanskrit गुर्जर (gurjara). Compare English Gujarati.

parole.significato: Knowledgeable, wise, intelligent.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi ज्ञानी (jñānī), from Sanskrit ज्ञानी (jñānī). Distantly related to know.

parole.significato: Synonym of turmeric.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi हलदी (haldī), from Sanskrit हरिद्रा (haridrā).

parole.significato: a salute or invocation towards the Hindu god Shiva, the god of destruction and time.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi हर हर महादेव (har har mahādev), from Sanskrit हर हर महादेव (hara hara mahādeva).

parole.significato: A pagoda, a type of gold coin.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi हून (hūn, “pagoda, a gold coin of Southern India”), from Sanskrit हून (hūna, “a kind of gold coin from a particular kingdom”).

parole.significato: One who opposes Hindutva and supports its enemies, a traitor, especially a race traitor.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi जयचन्द (jaycand) / जयचंद (jaycand), from Sanskrit जय (jaya, “victory”) + चन्द्र (candra, “moon”); the Hindi variant of Sanskrit जयचन्द्र (jayacandra, “Jayachandra”), a Gahadavala king whose rule immediately preceded the Ghurid Muslim conquest of much of India, and who was the acc

parole.significato: The people; the populace.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi जनता (jantā), from Sanskrit जनता (janatā).

parole.significato: A member of a people of northwestern India and Pakistan.
parole.testo: From Hindi जाट (jāṭ), ultimately from Sanskrit जर्तिक (jartika), of further unknown origin. Initially the name of a low-ranking tribe of Vahika (now in Punjab) mentioned in some Sanskrit-language Hindu texts such as the Mahabharata's Karna Parva, its descendant names, from Ashokan Prakrit *𑀚𑀝𑁆𑀝 (*ja

parole.significato: A grassy tamarisk shrub, of species Tamarix indica, common in river-marshes.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi झाऊ (jhāū), from Sanskrit झावु (jhāvu).

parole.significato: A member of an Indian caste historically found in Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, and other parts of north a…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi कलवार (kalvār), from Sanskrit कल्यपाल (kalyapāla), via Prakrit कल्लवाल (kallavāla).

parole.significato: A community of people living in northwestern India and Pakistan.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi कंबोज (kamboj), from Sanskrit कम्बोज (kamboja). Cf. Punjabi ਕੰਬੋਜ (kamboj, “Kamboj”).

parole.significato: Momordica charantia, the bitter melon or bitter gourd.
parole.testo: From Hindi करेला (karelā), from Sanskrit कारवेल्ल (kāravella).

parole.significato: Khichdi.
parole.testo: From Hindi खिचड़ी (khicṛī), from Sanskrit खिच्चा (khiccā). Compare khichdi.

parole.significato: center
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi केंद्र (kendra), from Sanskrit केन्द्र (kendra), from Ancient Greek κέντρον (kéntron), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱent-r-om (“a pointed tool”). Doublet of center.

parole.significato: A type of ancient South Asian castanet-like percussion instrument
parole.testo: From Hindi खड़ताल (khaṛtāl), itself originally derived from Sanskrit कर (kara, “hand”) + Sanskrit ताल (tāla, “clap”)

parole.significato: A cuckoo of the genus Eudynamys, native to Asia, Australia and the Pacific.
parole.testo: From Hindi कोयल (koyal), from Sanskrit कोकिल (kokila) which is of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: A red powder, made from saffron or turmeric, used ceremonially by Hindu women to make various markings on the body, esp…
parole.testo: From Hindi कुमकुम (kumkum) from Sanskrit कुङ्कुम (kuṅkuma).

parole.significato: A hot dust-bearing wind found in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and the Punjab.
parole.testo: From Hindi लू (lū), ultmately from Sanskrit उल्का (ulkā, “flame”).

parole.significato: A head or chief of a monastery.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi महान्त (mahānt), from Sanskrit महान् (mahān, “great”).

parole.significato: Synonym of mahout.
parole.testo: PIE word  *méǵh₂s Borrowed from Hindi महावत (mahāvat, “elephant keeper”), from Sanskrit महामात्र (mahāmātra, “elephant keeper; high official; king’s minister”), from महा (mahā, “great”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *méǵh₂s (“big, great”)) + मात्र (mātra, “measure; quantity”) (ultimately from

parole.significato: A time or moment considered lucky for beginning some project; an inauguration, now especially the start of a film produ…
parole.testo: From Hindi [Term?], from Sanskrit [Term?].

parole.significato: A member of a caste in South Asia whose traditional occupation is gardening; hence, any South Asian gardener.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi माली (mālī, “gardener”), from Sanskrit माली (mālī, “wreath-maker, garland-maker; florist; gardener”), मालिन् (mālin, “florist; gardener”), from माला (mālā, “wreath, garland; chaplet, crown”).

parole.significato: A traditional Hindu necklace tied around the bride's neck by the groom.
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Hindi मंगलसूत्र (maṅgalsūtra), ultimately from Sanskrit मंगलसूत्र (maṃgalasūtra, “auspicious thread”)

parole.significato: A member of a certain tribe of Rajasthan, India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi मीना (mīnā), from Sanskrit मीन (mīna, “fish, synonym of the patron deity Matsya”).

parole.significato: fenugreek
parole.testo: From Hindi मेथी (methī), from Sanskrit मेथिका (methikā), ultimately from Proto-Dravidian *mentti (“fenugreek”).

parole.significato: A village chief or leader of a panchayat in parts of India and Nepal.
parole.testo: From Hindi, from Sanskrit.

parole.significato: free, unconstrained
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi मुक्त (mukt).

parole.significato: mung bean (Vigna radiata, syn. Phaseolus aureus), cultivated for its sprouts.
parole.testo: From Hindi मूँग (mūṅg), from Sanskrit मुद्ग (mudga).

parole.significato: Any of group of nine public-sector undertakings in India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi नवरत्न (navratna), from Sanskrit नवरत्न (navaratna).

parole.significato: An anklet.
parole.testo: From Hindi नूपुर (nūpur, “anklet, nupur, ornament for the feet”), from Sanskrit नूपुर (nūpura, “anklet”).

parole.significato: Spinach or similar greens (including Amaranthus species and Chenopodium album).
parole.testo: From Hindi पालक (pālak), from Sanskrit पालक्या (pālakyā).

parole.significato: A tree of eastern India and Burma, Butea monosperma.
parole.testo: From Hindi पलाश (palāś), from Sanskrit.

parole.significato: Synonym of palanquin.
parole.testo: From Hindi पालकी (pālkī), from Sanskrit पल्यङ्क (palyaṅka, “bed, couch, litter”) of uncertain origin. Doublet of palanquin.

parole.significato: The usually decorated end of a sari that hangs loose when worn.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi पल्लू (pallū), from पल्ला (pallā, “side”), from Sanskrit पल्ल (palla). Compare with palla.

parole.significato: A former low-denomination coin of northern India.
parole.testo: From Hindi पाई (pāī, “low-denomination coin”), from Sanskrit पादिका (pādikā, “foot, shoe”), from पाद (pāda, “foot, base, quarter”) + -इक (-ika, “-ic: forming adjectives”).

parole.significato: A state (administrative division) of the Republic of India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi प्रदेश (pradeś).

parole.significato: The footprint or pawprint of an animal; a pugmark.
parole.testo: The noun is borrowed from Hindi पग (pag, “step; (less common) foot; leg”), from Old Hindi पगु (pagu), from Sanskrit पद्ग (padga), from पद् (pad, “step; foot”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ped- (“to step; to walk; to fall; to stumble”)) + ग (ga, stem at the ends of compounds denoting going o

parole.significato: A fan, particularly a large fan made of leaf or cloth and hung from the ceiling, (historical) formerly often operated b…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi पंखा (paṅkhā, “fan”), from Sanskrit पक्षक (pakṣaka), from पक्ष (pakṣa, “wing”).

parole.significato: A family priest.
parole.testo: From Hindi पुरोहित (purohit), from Sanskrit पुरोहित (purohita) from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰey-.

parole.significato: A strip of cloth wound round the leg, worn for protection or support by hikers, soldiers etc.
parole.testo: From Hindi पट्टी (paṭṭī, “bandage, strip of cloth”), from Sanskrit पट्टिका (paṭṭikā) of similar meaning.

parole.significato: Synonym of stray dog, particularly in Indian contexts.
parole.testo: From Hindi पाहि (pāhi, “migrant farmer, passer-through”), from Sanskrit पार्श्व (pārśva, “side, vicinity”).

parole.significato: A member of the kshatriya Hindu caste in India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi राजपूत (rājpūt), from Sanskrit राजपुत्र (rājaputra, “prince”), a compound of राजन् (rājan, “king”) and पुत्र (putra, “son”). See also the related term Fitzroy.

parole.significato: An ornamental cotton wristband tied by a girl or woman on to the wrist of her brother, or of one who takes on the respo…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi राखी (rākhī, “a rakhi”), from Sanskrit रक्षिका (rakṣikā, “a rakhi”), from रक्षा (rakṣā, “care, guarding, preservation, protection; a rakhi”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂lek- (“to protect”).

parole.significato: A geometric or stylized design on the floor (or other flat surface) made using small coloured granules, powder or flowe…
parole.testo: From Hindi रंगोली (raṅgolī), from Sanskrit रङ्ग (raṅga, “colour”).

parole.significato: horoscope, particularly one derived from Indian astronomy
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi राशिफल (rāśiphal), in turn borrowed from Sanskrit राशिफल (rāśiphala), from राशि (rāśi, “zodiac sign”) + फल (phala, “outcome, result”)

parole.significato: A Burmese carriage of state.
parole.testo: From Hindi रथ (rath), from Sanskrit रथ (ratha).

parole.significato: A saline efflorescence that comes to the surface on the usar plains of northern India, particularly in Uttar Pradesh.
parole.testo: From Hindi रेह (reh, “salt marsh”); compare Sanskrit रेणु (reṇu, “grain of salt, dust, powder”).

parole.significato: A freshwater fish, Labeo rohita, of the carp family, found throughout Asia.
parole.testo: From Hindi रोहू (rohū), from Sanskrit रोहित (rohita, “reddish”), due to the reddish tint of the fish's fins.

parole.significato: A person who belongs to a monotheistic sect of Hinduism, having beliefs similar to those of Quakers.
parole.testo: From Hindi साध (sādh, “member of the Sadh sect; Sadh”), from Sanskrit साधु (sādhu).

parole.significato: A soldier.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi सैनिक (sainik), from Sanskrit सैनिक (sainika).

parole.significato: Shorea robusta, a dipterocarpaceous tree.
parole.testo: From Hindi साल (sāl), from Sanskrit शाल (śāla).

parole.significato: A Southeast Asian deer (Rusa unicolor).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi सांभर (sāmbhar), साँभर (sāmbhar), from Sanskrit शम्बर (śambara, “a kind of deer”).

parole.significato: A gathering for the purpose of singing songs; a musical ceremony.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi संगीत (saṅgīt), from Sanskrit संगीत (saṃgīta), from सम्- (sam-, “together”) + गीत (gīta, “song”).

parole.significato: A man in the stage of sannyasa; a wandering ascetic, a religious mendicant.
parole.testo: Via Hindi संन्यासी (sannyāsī), ultimately from Sanskrit संन्यासिन् (saṃnyāsin).

parole.significato: Any of several species of sugarcane or sugarcane-like grasses found in India, of the genera Saccharum and Tripidium.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi सरपत (sarpat), from Sanskrit शर (śara, “arrow, reed”) + पत्त्र (pattra, “leaf”).

parole.significato: Flour made from a mixture of ground pulses and cereals.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi सत्तू (sattū), from Sanskrit सक्तु (saktu).

parole.significato: A member of the Savarna gotra (lineage) of the Brahmin caste.
parole.testo: From Hindi सवर्ण (savarṇ), derived from Sanskrit सवर्ण (savarṇa, “same colour, same caste”).

parole.significato: In Indian traditions: a disciple who receives spiritual knowledge from a guru.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi शिष्य (śiṣya, “disciple, student”), from Sanskrit शिष्य (śiṣya), from Sanskrit शास् (śās, “to teach, instruct”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱeh₁s- (“to teach, to indicate”).

parole.significato: urotherapy
parole.testo: From Hindi शिवांबु (śivāmbu), from Sanskrit शिवाम्बु (śivāmbu), from शिव (śiva, “Shiva”) + अम्बु (ambu, “water”).

parole.significato: The water caltrop.
